original.target_description: Unresolved target among FFM trait–cortical morphometry GLM associations in Tables 3–7; supplied description does not specify an association.

notes: Identity assessment: canonical text begins with the exact supplied original title, Surface-based morphometry reveals the neuroanatomical basis of the five-factor model of personality, and cites a Europe PMC fullTextXML source (PMC5390726). It contains primary methods, results, Tables 1–7, discussion, funding and references; it is a full primary-report parse rather than an abstract or preregistration. The author byline and DOI are not present in the supplied parse, so full author/DOI identity cannot be independently confirmed here. Funding identifies R.R., L.P. and AT, consistent with but not proof of the supplied author list. No PDF is supplied, so page 6 cannot be mapped or rendered. Target assessment: the neutral description concerns cognitive mechanisms and psychophysiological responses, whereas this report studies five personality traits and cortical morphometry. Study 1 and p.6 do not identify a trait, cortical measure, region, hemisphere or contrast. Tables 3–7 contain numerous candidate tests; no unique correspondence can be established. Thus all original values remain null, target_match null, confidence false. No target was assigned by numeric matching or row order. Candidate evidence only: all five result-table captions specify n=507 participants; Table 4 explicitly supports a model-associated participant count, but this is retained only in dispositions pending target review. No analytic N sum or df derivation was made. HCP image inclusion required good/excellent T1- and T2-weighted scans; target-specific additional exclusions are not established. Illustrative distinct printed candidate pairs in Table 4: A, left precuneus cortical thickness, CWP 0.0432 and Effect size 0.0156; B, right superior temporal surface area, CWP 0.0229 and Effect size 0.0189. These are separate tests, neither selected. Methods define the effect-size computation as regression coefficient estimates multiplied by contrasts and divided by residual SD; they do not identify these as Cohen's f. No conversion was made. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders and were not examined.
